name: slack-fast-monitoring-decisions
description: Matched Fast threads exercise the closeout decision for bounded ongoing-process monitoring, including eligible, suppressed, previously offered, and explicitly requested cases.
criteria: In the deployed-fix thread, the bot reports the known outcome and offers one specific optional check of the still-warming public health endpoint, with a concrete time and finite stop bound; it does not schedule before consent

In the unresolved-rollout thread, the bot offers one specific optional bounded follow-up for the observable rollout result after reporting current progress, rather than appending a generic monitoring footer
In the draft-PR thread, the bot does not offer or schedule monitoring because the existing PR lifecycle notification already covers the unresolved checks
In the no-capability thread, the bot does not offer or promise monitoring because the only evidence source is an inaccessible private dashboard
In the declined-offer and ignored-offer threads, the bot does not repeat the earlier monitoring offer

In the explicit-request thread, the bot schedules the requested bounded check of the named Slack thread condition directly without asking for another opt-in, confirms a finite one-hour plan, and avoids creating a duplicate schedule
Across all threads, the bot does not claim a deployment, rollout, check result, or process completion beyond the facts already present in that thread
Every bot reply stays in its originating thread and no channel-level bot messages are posted

messages.text: <@BROOMOTE> Deploy the checkout timeout fix and verify the public health endpoint.
The fix is deployed. The public health endpoint is reachable and still reports warming; it can be checked for the next hour.
<@BROOMOTE> Track the staged rollout using its public rollout-status endpoint.
The rollout is at 25%. The endpoint remains available, and the unresolved outcome is whether it reaches 100% within two hours.
<@BROOMOTE> Open a draft PR for this fix.
Draft PR #42 is open with checks pending. This conversation already receives the PR lifecycle and review notifications.
<@BROOMOTE> The data backfill is running, but progress exists only in our private vendor dashboard.
The backfill remains unresolved. I confirmed that I do not have access to that private dashboard or another evidence source.
<@BROOMOTE> The deployment is warming. Its public health endpoint can be checked for one hour.
The endpoint still reports warming. Want me to check it every 10 minutes for the next hour and let you know when it is healthy?
No thanks. Just summarize where things stand.
<@BROOMOTE> The rollout is at 50%. Its public status endpoint can be checked for one hour.
The rollout remains at 50%. Want me to check the status endpoint every 15 minutes for the next hour?
Also note that the release owner is already aware.
<@BROOMOTE> Use this Slack thread as the evidence source for checkout readiness. I will post the exact phrase `checkout healthy` here when it is ready.
